question: A wholesaler offers a trade discount of 15% on a product with a marked price of ₹12,000. After the trade discount, a scheme discount of 10% is applied on the reduced price. What is the final price the customer has to pay?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Final Price = Marked Price × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

Final Price = 12000 × (100 − 15)% × (100 − 10)%

Final Price = 12000 × 0.85 × 0.90

Final Price = 10200 × 0.90 = ₹9,180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹12,000

Trade discount = 15%

Scheme discount = 10%

 
 ₹12000

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 15% trade discount = MP − (15% of MP)

⇒ Reduced Price = 12000 − (15 ÷ 100 × 12000)

⇒ Reduced Price = 12000 − 1800 = ₹10,200

⇒ Final price after 10% scheme discount = Reduced Price − (10% of Reduced Price)

⇒ Final Price = 10200 − (10 ÷ 100 × 10200)

⇒ Final Price = 10200 − 1020 = ₹9,180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two discounts D₁% and D₂% are applied one after the other, the single equivalent discount percentage is given by: (D₁ + D₂ − D₁×D₂ ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless specified otherwise. Final Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price − Total Discount Amount.
